payload.name: pc-check-retry-eligibility
payload.description: Deterministic pure-logic guard that returns whether a logical step invocation is eligible for a bounded retry, before any dispatch is considered. It is evidence-conditioned pure logic, not dispatch permission: it never grants Tool permission, does not replace live instance-wide Tool policy, current global allow/block settings, cancellation, stale-attempt fencing, resource limits or actual deduplication evidence. It only reports eligibility from declared inputs; a true result still requires a fresh valid attempt and current policy admission at the actual dispatch boundary. Missing, null or invalid data fails closed. Typed inputs are a target interface; the typed-runner and Monty execution gap remain an explicit prerequisite. No I/O, imports or host calls.

composition_summary: Proposed one class-22 pure-logic component pc-check-retry-eligibility. It reads raw candidate inputs with presence/type checks (operation_state, outcome, attempt, max_attempts, read_only, dedup_verified) and returns {'retry': boolean} at module scope, failing closed on missing/null/invalid data. True only when outcome is retryable, attempt < max_attempts, state is not completed, and read_only OR dedup_verified is true. Completed effects never replay. The body makes zero host calls and no I/O/imports. The description retains the live policy/cancellation/resource checks and typed-runner gap; this guard is evidence-conditioned pure logic, not dispatch permission. No adjusted volatile messages, bridge messages, recipe updates, intent examples or settings changes were made; the volatile tail was preserved unchanged.
